title: Both engines write the same word, and contracts converges
description: The ts engine changes to write "completed", matching PGE and the 218-of-250 on-disk majority. This is the change that makes the two engines agree about what happened, and it closes the contracts divergence.

successCriteria.description: runSprintCycle writes "completed" where it wrote "passed" (src/orchestrator/pipeline.ts:589), and every ts-side consumer of that write follows — including the split at :1052 and the workflow flusher and interpreter readers.

The contracts conformance divergence's STATUS delta is closed. The other two field deltas (evaluatorFeedback, generatorNotes) are either closed too or recorded with a stated reason — say which, and do not leave it ambiguous.
src/pge/nodes/sprint-evaluate.test.ts, which pins the current write, is edited deliberately rather than incidentally.
The replay golden cases are re-captured and the diff is verified confined to the status word, the version field and their direct consequences. Anything else moving is a STOP CONDITION.
The replay count stays at or above GOLDEN_MIN_REPLAY_CASES and no case is relabelled from replay to integrity.
The negative controls in the golden suite are re-verified to still bite at the current case count — the previous spec found three that had silently stopped biting as the dataset grew.
Full suite, typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build green.

nonGoals: Changing what the evaluator DECIDES. This sprint changes the word recorded for an outcome, never the outcome.
stopConditions: Re-capture shows a field moving that is not the status, the version, or a direct consequence — stop and report.
Closing the status delta does not close the contracts divergence because another delta remains — that is a finding to record, not to force.
definitionOfDone: All required criteria met, the full suite plus typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build green, the golden gate passing, and every documentation claim added backed by a test that fails when the claim stops being true.
generatorNotes: This is the behaviour-changing sprint and the one a careless blanket-replace would damage. The ts engine has several readers of its own write (pipeline.ts:1052, workflow/flusher.ts:62,76, workflow/interpreter.ts:128,134,140,141) — note that some of those read an OUTCOME field rather than a contract status; check each. Sprint 1's predicate should already cover most reader sites; what changes here is the WRITE. Re-capture in this sprint, not the next — the previous spec learned that deferring a blast radius makes the suite red in between.
evaluatorNotes: Verify the divergence set by running the conformance harness yourself, not by reading the pin. Confirm the status delta is genuinely gone rather than masked. For sc-5-4, read every re-captured diff hunk — the previous spec's sprint 5 found a case affected for a reason nobody predicted, and the discipline that caught it was reading the diff rather than trusting the count. For sc-5-6, revert one negative control to its pre-sprint form and confirm it now produces a false pass, which is how the previous spec proved its controls were strengthened.
